Although the exact number of people killed during the outbreak is a source of debate, the generally accepted number is in the 300–350 range.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-192) 271 of those deaths occurred on April 27, the date of peak activity.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:1-103)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-193)

The high number of fatalities on April 27 was studied in detail following the event. Despite 92 tornado warnings being issued for Alabama,[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-194) 271 people were killed, many in poorly built homes.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-:1-103) In a study of people killed during the outbreak published by the [American Journal of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Journal_of_Public_Health "American Journal of Public Health"), it was determined that only 102, or 41.3%, out of the 247 victims studied received a warning.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-195): e5–e6  It was determined that the majority of fatalities during the outbreak happened because of a lack of adequate community shelters in rural communities throughout Alabama.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-196)

### Immediate recovery efforts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2011_Super_Outbreak&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: Immediate recovery efforts")]

Alabama Governor [Robert J. Bentley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_J._Bentley "Robert J. Bentley") declared a state of emergency in the state of Alabama on April 27, due to storm damage from severe thunderstorms earlier that day as well as forthcoming severe weather later that day. States of emergency were also declared in Arkansas, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), Mississippi, Missouri, [Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee "Tennessee"), and Oklahoma because of the flooding and tornadoes.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-197) Following the tornado outbreak on the evening of April 27, [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") granted a federal emergency declaration for the state of Alabama, giving federal assistance, including search and rescue assets, to the affected region.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-198)

More than 2,000 [National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Guard_of_the_United_States "National Guard of the United States") troops were deployed to Alabama, assisting local and state first responders in search and rescue efforts.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-199) President Obama visited the affected areas of Alabama on April 29.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-200) Also on April 29, he approved a federal disaster declaration for seven Mississippi counties: [Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarke_County,_Mississippi "Clarke County, Mississippi"), [Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greene_County,_Mississippi "Greene County, Mississippi"), [Hinds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinds_County,_Mississippi "Hinds County, Mississippi"), [Jasper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasper_County,_Mississippi "Jasper County, Mississippi"), [Kemper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kemper_County,_Mississippi "Kemper County, Mississippi"), [Lafayette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lafayette_County,_Mississippi "Lafayette County, Mississippi"), and [Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_County,_Mississippi "Monroe County, Mississippi").[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-201)

Storms through the area severely damaged [Tennessee Valley Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Valley_Authority "Tennessee Valley Authority") (TVA)'s [power grid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_power_transmission "Electric power transmission") for transmitting electricity throughout the region. More than 300 power transmission towers, 120 to 150 feet (37 to 46 m) tall, were destroyed in the storms, some "twisted like bow ties" according to National Weather Service meteorologist Eric Holweg. The towers supported some 90 transmission lines, a mixture of 500[kV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volt "Volt") and 161kV lines. Those lines provided power from TVA to 128 regional distributors.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-202)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-bowTieTower-203)

[![Image 406: An electrical tower is bent in an arched shape against a blue sky](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Electric_line_tower.jpg/250px-Electric_line_tower.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Electric_line_tower.jpg)

Transmission tower bent near [Huntsville, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntsville,_Alabama "Huntsville, Alabama").

TVA lost the ability to transmit power from both [Browns Ferry Nuclear Power Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Browns_Ferry_Nuclear_Power_Plant "Browns Ferry Nuclear Power Plant") and [Widows Creek Fossil Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Widows_Creek_Power_Plant "Widows Creek Power Plant") after the storms on April 27, requiring both to be shut down. The nuclear plant's [cold shutdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shutdown_(nuclear_reactor) "Shutdown (nuclear reactor)") was supported by diesel generators for four days until a second 161kV line could be restored to the plant. The loss of redundant off-site power required a "notification of unusual event", the lowest of four levels of concern dictated by the [NRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_Regulatory_Commission "Nuclear Regulatory Commission"). Some 60 percent of the sirens for warning residents of worse problems around Browns Ferry were disabled by the storms, and the plant had to arrange plans to use cars with loudspeakers to warn residents in case of another problem.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-TFP-nuke-110)[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-bowTieTower-203) The Nuclear Regulatory Commission stated at a press conference: "The plants' conditions are stable and are being placed in a cooled-down condition."[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-UPI-nuke-204)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-205)

[Huntsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntsville,_Alabama "Huntsville, Alabama") was the largest city with no electricity from TVA.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-bowTieTower-203) All the traffic lights were off, a dusk-to-dawn curfew was imposed, students were sent home from [United States Space Camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Space_Camp "United States Space Camp"), and the [Panoply Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panoply_Arts_Festival "Panoply Arts Festival") was canceled.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-206)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-207)[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-208) Power was restored gradually to Huntsville, beginning with 3 percent on the morning of May 1.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-3percent-209) Only localized outages remained eight days after the storm.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-210) In addition to traffic and safety issues, the outage caused difficulties with water treatment and distribution and retail of all kinds, including [gasoline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasoline "Gasoline") and food purchases.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-3percent-209)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-211)

Ontario electricity outages were minor, mostly caused by the windstorms of April 28. Although they affected thousands of people at different times throughout the day, all power was restored by the end of the day.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-ottawacitizen.com-187)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-theweathernetwork.com-188)[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Fierce_winds_whip_through_Ontario-189)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-JMontreal-190)[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Super_Outbreak#cite_note-Zone-911-191)
